title: Check yourself: accessing fields, methods and constructors

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A reporting service starts with `--add-opens java.base/java.util=ALL-UNNAMED`. Its reflective deep-copy helper copies Strings as they are; for any other object it calls `setAccessible(true)` on every instance field, inherited and primitive ones included. It is handed an object of the service's own class holding a `LinkedHashMap<String, java.time.Duration>` with two entries. What happens?

options.text: The copy completes, since the flag reaches every package of java.base and no module stays closed
options.says: --add-opens names one package; opening java.util moved the page's failure on to java.time

options.text: The copy fails at the first Duration, since the flag reaches java.util and no other package
options.says: the grant is per package, and Duration's private fields are in java.time, which nobody opened

options.text: The copy fails at the map itself, since the flag reaches public members and no private ones
options.says: with java.util opened, the page's dump read ArrayList's private elementData and size

options.text: The copy completes minus the Durations, since setAccessible skips the fields no flag reaches
options.says: setAccessible throws InaccessibleObjectException; trySetAccessible is the one that returns false

origin.section: setAccessible Opens Your Own Classes, and java.base Only One Granted Package at a Time

questions.stem: `class Quota { private final int perMinute = 600; private final int burst; Quota(int burst) { this.burst = burst; } int perMinute() { return perMinute; } int burst() { return burst; } }`. A test builds `new Quota(20)`, makes both fields accessible, sets `perMinute` to 60 and `burst` to 5 with `Field.set`, then prints `quota.perMinute()` and `quota.burst()`. What does it print?

options.text: 60 and 5, since both writes succeed and each getter reads its own field
options.says: javac compiled the constant 600 into perMinute(), which never reads the field

options.text: 600 and 5, since both writes succeed and one getter returns a copy javac made
options.says: a final field initialised with a constant expression is inlined by javac; the constructor-assigned field is read with getfield

options.text: 60 and 20, since both writes succeed and one getter returns a copy the constructor made
options.says: the constructor-assigned field changed for its getter on the page (backoffMs: getter 800); only the constant was copied, by javac

options.text: 600 and 20, since both writes succeed and each getter returns a copy made at construction
options.says: the getter of a constructor-assigned field read the new value on the page (backoffMs: getter 800); only the constant initialiser was copied, by javac

origin.section: A Final Instance Field Can Be Written, and Code Compiled Against Its Constant Never Sees It

questions.stem: A price cache holds `record Price(String sku, long cents)` objects. A one-off repair job corrects wrong prices in place: it gets the `cents` field, calls `setAccessible(true)` on it, then `set(price, corrected)`. The job runs on Java 21 from the class path. What happens?

options.text: The write goes through, since setAccessible(true) gives write access to any final field that isn't static
options.says: the Field.set javadoc excludes record classes, and the page's write to Money.cents was refused

options.text: The write goes through but price.cents() keeps the old value, since javac compiled the value into the accessor
options.says: the write never happens; and only constant expressions are inlined, not values passed to a constructor

options.text: The job fails in set with IllegalAccessException, since a record's fields refuse writes even when accessible
options.says: setAccessible succeeds and set refuses, as for Money.cents on the page

options.text: The job fails in setAccessible with InaccessibleObjectException, since a record's fields can't be made accessible
options.says: setAccessible succeeded on the record's field; InaccessibleObjectException is about packages a module doesn't open

origin.section: A Static Final Field and a Record Component Refuse the Write

questions.stem: A job scheduler runs each job's `execute()` with `Method.invoke`. Around the call it has `catch (IllegalStateException e) { markSkipped(job); } catch (ReflectiveOperationException e) { markFailed(job); }`. One job's `execute()` throws `IllegalStateException("lock held")`. What does the scheduler do?

options.text: It marks the job skipped, since an unchecked exception from the job leaves invoke unchanged
options.says: invoke wraps checked and unchecked exceptions alike

options.text: It marks the job failed, since the job's exception leaves invoke as the cause of a wrapper
options.says: the IllegalStateException arrives inside InvocationTargetException, a ReflectiveOperationException

options.text: Neither catch runs, since the job's exception leaves invoke as an UndeclaredThrowableException
options.says: UndeclaredThrowableException comes from a dynamic proxy (unit 9.2.3), not from Method.invoke

options.text: Neither catch runs, since the job's exception leaves invoke as an IllegalArgumentException
options.says: invoke throws IllegalArgumentException only for arguments that don't fit; the method's own exception is wrapped

origin.section: Method.invoke Wraps the Method's Exceptions and Throws Its Own Argument Errors Unwrapped

concepts: --add-opens (or Add-Opens in an executable jar's manifest) opens one package of a module, so opening java.util leaves java.time closed.
Field.set writes a final instance field of an ordinary class after setAccessible, but code compiled against a constant initialiser keeps the old value because javac inlined it.
